title: The General Arrives
summary: At a temporary Los Lagartos camp in Cinder Basin, an itinerant brotherhood greets Kael as General Saye, the absent authority whose return is supposed to settle a bitter succession dispute. Kael's attempt to pass through only increases their certainty.

panelPlan.text: Wide camp beneath patched shade cloths and the ribs of a half-buried Sunforge. Los Lagartos stop eating, gambling and arguing when Kael, Eva and Jessa enter.
An older member stands and addresses Kael as General Saye. Several others rise with relief; a rival cluster rises with anger.
Kael keeps walking toward the water table. Jessa quietly changes direction toward the exit. Eva slows down because this is exactly why she came.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not your general.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I imagine he did. I'm still not him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Can we get some water and keep moving?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: That's the first sensible thing anyone has said.

directionInline.text: Los Lagartos are a community, not faceless militia. Their recognition matters because they have built a social expectation around Saye's return.

title: A Vote Nobody Wants
summary: Los Lagartos insist that 'Saye' settle whether the group follows an older blood claim or a younger elected leader. Kael refuses to choose, but every refusal is interpreted as the general testing them.

panelPlan.text: Two sides of the camp face each other across a long communal table. Kael has been placed at the head despite repeatedly moving his chair sideways.
Speakers from both sides make concise cases. Eva watches the group more than Kael, noticing how everyone edits themselves in his presence.
Kael finally stands, moves the head chair out of the way and sits on a water crate at the side, physically refusing the role.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can't. Neither claim has anything to do with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: It's the only one I have.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That doesn't seem to be helping.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: The gun on the table bothers me. Their opinion of my teaching style does not.

directionInline.text: The mistaken identity is socially consequential. Kael's refusal itself becomes material the community interprets.

title: The Woman Behind Them
summary: Eva notices Veyra questioning camp members about Kael. Veyra reveals that she already has more identities attached to Kael's face than Eva and Jessa have encountered, making clear that her investigation predates their awareness of it.

panelPlan.text: At the edge of camp, Veyra interviews a Lagarto quietly while writing nothing down. Eva watches from behind a shade post; Jessa catches Eva watching.
Veyra turns and catches Eva's stare. She approaches rather than pretending she was not observing them.
Jessa steps between them only enough to make the boundary clear. Veyra looks past her toward Kael at the communal table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: How long has he been calling himself Kael?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Since before I met him, I assume.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I have four names attached to that face. I think that deserves a better question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Then ask him instead of us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: He doesn't answer the question I'm asking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He answers. You just keep wanting a different answer.

directionInline.text: Veyra's reference to four names is deliberate foreshadowing: she has been collecting candidate identities and local stories before the trio understands the scope of her pursuit. Do not imply she knows the deeper cause.

title: What Saye Would Do
summary: A confrontation inside Los Lagartos turns violent when one claimant tries to force the decision. Kael intervenes to prevent a killing, and the group immediately treats his action as Saye's judgment.

panelPlan.text: A younger Lagarto draws on an older rival across the campfire. People freeze because any intervention will be read as taking a side.
Kael knocks the muzzle aside with a tin cup before the shot clears leather. Sand Rider, a real local scout, pins the shooter's wrist without ceremony.
The crowd looks to Kael for the verdict. Kael looks at Sand Rider, then at the two claimants, irritated that stopping a murder has become constitutional law.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No. I stopped him from shooting somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't care what Saye always did. I'm not Saye.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Then you're going to keep having this problem.

directionInline.text: Sand Rider is a grounded local figure and is not the later distant Rider mystery. Keep the action social and human.

title: No General
summary: Kael turns the group's need for Saye back on them: if they cannot choose without a dead man's authority, then Saye's return would only postpone the fight. The community makes its own decision while Kael prepares to leave.

panelPlan.text: Kael stands outside the head position at the table and returns the old general's signet or token that someone pressed into his hand.
The two claimant groups face each other without Kael between them. Jessa has the rig ready; Eva lingers close enough to hear.
One Lagarto moves the head chair away entirely. Others follow, reshaping the circle rather than crowning a winner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm not your general. If I leave and you still can't decide this, what exactly have I settled?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. Ask somebody who knew him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't planning to say anything else.

directionInline.text: Kael does not solve governance or prescribe a better system. He only refuses to be the missing authority, forcing the people who live there to own their choice.

title: A Name in the Dust
summary: As the trio leaves Cinder Basin, Eva learns that Los Lagartos were told to expect General Saye by a traveling preacher several days earlier. Veyra watches the departure from behind them, making the pattern feel less accidental without yet proving coordination.

panelPlan.text: The rig pulls away from camp. Eva runs alongside for two steps after asking one last question, then catches the rear rail.
She tells Kael and Jessa that a preacher described Saye before their arrival. Jessa looks back through the dust.
Far behind, Veyra stands where the camp road narrows, not following yet. Near her, a black Sunforge rib catches the light. Kael never looks back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: A preacher told them to expect Saye.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And he said Saye would pretend not to know them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: All right. That one bothers me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: It still doesn't prove the preacher knew me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You loaded his bag before he agreed to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can hear both of you.

directionInline.text: The recurrence becomes harder to dismiss, but no one has proof of a coordinated scheme. The Sunforge is visual recurrence only; nobody attributes causality.
